text:
sam: Quick question about the new /v1/generate endpoint auth behavior — if a request includes both `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `x-api-key: <key>`, which should we prefer? Want to avoid surprising older clients. cc @erin @mohit

erin: prefer Authorization bearer if present. it's the modern standard and lets us reuse oauth-like validation flows (scopes, expiry). fallback to x-api-key for legacy clients. :+1:

mohit: agreed. also need clear precedence for org/project scoping headers. if `x-org-id` is present but the api key is scoped to a different org, do we reject? i'm leaning to reject with 403 (scope mismatch) rather than silently map.

sam: makes sense. so rules: 1) pick Authorization Bearer if present 2) otherwise x-api-key 3) validate key -> check org/project scope -> return 403 if mismatch.

erin: yep. error shapes: return 401 for missing/invalid credentials, 403 for valid creds but insufficient scope, 400 only for malformed header. include machine-readable code in body, e.g. `{ "error": "insufficient_scope", "code": "auth_insufficient_scope" }`. we should standardize codes across endpoints.

julia: from product/customer side — we need a deprecation plan for `x-api-token` (legacy header). are we translating it today?

mohit: currently runtime accepts `x-api-token` as alias for `x-api-key`. we should emit a warning header when it's used and schedule deprecation in 3 months. e.g. `Deprecation-Warning: x-api-token will be removed on 2026-06-01`.

sasha: would prefer we also log a distinct metric for legacy header usage so support can surface affected customers.

erin: good call. add metric `auth.legacy_header.x_api_token.count` and tag by org.

sam: about key rotation — what do we expect? if a client rotates keys using our API (create new, then delete old), we might see a short period where both keys exist. we should support two active keys per account by default?

mohit: runtime already supports multiple active keys per org/project. main requirement is eventual consistency: deletion might take a few seconds to propagate to all nodes. prefer graceful 409? i'd rather return 401 for deleted key (explicit invalid) and let retry be a fresh auth. we should document the propagation window (~30s).

erin: from security: avoid 2xx with warning when key is about to be revoked. if a token is revoked, treat as invalid immediately. but for rotation we rely on users creating new token first then swapping their clients. include recommended flow in docs.

sam: sample curl we'll add to docs for precedence and scope check:
```
# preferred
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "x-org-id: org_123" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# legacy fallback
curl -H "x-api-key: $API_KEY" -H "x-org-id: org_123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

julia: what about ambiguous cases: different keys in Authorization vs x-api-key? which wins?

erin: reject with 400 (conflicting-credentials). don't try to resolve two different identities in one request. include `code: auth_conflicting_credentials`.

mohit: also enforce single org header. if `x-org-id` doesn't match key's default org, and the key is multi-org-scoped, validate explicit header. otherwise if header missing, default to key's org.

sasha: ci-bot picked up a failing test `auth-header-tests` on canary that expects 200 when both headers present (x-api-key + Authorization with same key). cc-ing @ci-bot

ci-bot: Test auth-header-tests failed on canary-3. Failing assertion: response.code == 200. See job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/1234.

mohit: thanks. failing because our canary code currently preferred x-api-key over Authorization. i'll flip precedence in runtime config and run canary again.

sam: for rollout plan: flip precedence in canary (5% traffic) for 24h, monitor `auth.failure.401`, `auth.conflict.400` and legacy usage metric. if stable, increase to 25% then 100% over 48h. add feature flag `auth.header_precedence=authorization_first` so we can rollback quickly.

erin: add a policy doc note that when both headers are present and identical it's allowed (200). if different -> 400. deprecation: announce x-api-token removal in 3 months, but keep x-api-key forever (no deprecation).

julia: i'll draft the customer-facing changelog and migration notes. ping me when canary is green.

mohit: re-ran canary after flip, tests passing. will push increment.

sam: thanks team — i'll update the API docs snippet and open the rollout PR. :eyes:
